title: An Application of Cluster Analysis and Multidimensional Scaling to the Question of ‘Hands’ and ‘Languages’ in the Voynich Manuscript
summary: D'Imperio used glyph counts for the first roughly 350–400 transcribed characters on each of 40 pages to compare four clustering procedures and a multidimensional scaling procedure. Four outputs grouped Biological B pages with Herbal B page 59 in Currier's numbering, and the author identified the narrow range of sampled sections as a limit on separating subject, handwriting, and the A/B grouping.
established: The samples were 16 Herbal A, 12 Herbal B, and 12 Biological B pages according to Currier's classifications in Figure 6 (pp. 64, 75).

PEP-1, HICLUS, and Ling's (K,R) algorithm used correlations between single-glyph count profiles. Those clusterings and the MINISSA placement put the Biological B pages together with Herbal B page 59, whereas the Manhattan-distance TAXMAP-2 result clearly grouped ten Biological B pages (pp. 65–69).

The author interpreted the horizontal MINISSA coordinate as associated with Currier A/B. The secondary coordinate could reflect either the Herbal/Biological section contrast or the Hand B/Hand Z contrast, which coincided for the B pages sampled (p. 69).

open.question: Does the clustering of D'Imperio's 40-page panel, including the association of Currier page 59 with Biological B, hold across modern independent transliterations and comparable text windows?
open.check: Document a Currier-number-to-locus crosswalk for Figure 6 and all exclusions. On public practice data compare correlation and length-normalized Manhattan distance on the first 350–400 transcribed glyphs in ZL and IT. Repeat for matching later windows where long enough. Report within-group and between-group distances and the nearest group for page 59, using physical folios as blocks. On a broader public sample report the support for section contrasts within modern hands separately before interpreting the B-only grouping.
